answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 14 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The river multiplier is published, charged in cipher, and zenith lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 592 identities would post 3256 proofs and burn roughly 20 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
